#6808. Butternut Pasta With Sausage and Dates

Squash and sausage are a heroic autumnal pairing, especially in a weeknight-friendly pasta. Butternut is the easiest squash to source—not to mention easily found peeled and chopped (a blessing for those with more timid knife skills). But other winter squash like acorn or red kuri can stand in as desired. Whichever squash you select, a sharp, heavy chef’s knife is best for breaking down the chunky veg. But to make your life easier, microwave the squash for 1 to 2 minutes. It will slightly soften, making it simpler—and safer—to slice through.

Rigatoni’s ribbed surface and large holes help chunky squash sauce cling and bites of seared sausage and date wedge—opting for a nutty whole wheat variety will only add to this meal’s autumnal earthiness.

More cozy pastas this way: Balsamic Mushroom and Sausage Pasta; Creamy Red Curry Pasta; and Baked Feta Pasta With Green Sauce.

Cook 1 medium butternut squash (1½–2 lb.), peeled, halved, seeds removed, cut into 1" pieces (about 6 cups), in a large pot of boiling salted water until very tender, 12–14 minutes. Using a slotted spoon, transfer squash to a medium bowl. Reduce heat to low, cover pot, and leave on burner to keep warm.

Heat 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a large high-sided skillet or a medium Dutch oven over medium-high. Add 1 lb. hot or sweet Italian sausage, casings removed, and break up into small pieces with a wooden spoon. Cook, undisturbed, until deeply browned underneath, about 3 minutes. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until browned all over and just cooked through, 3–4 minutes more. Transfer to a plate with a slotted spoon.

Reduce heat to medium-low. Cook 3½ oz. Medjool dates (about 6), pitted, sliced lengthwise ¾" thick, in same pan, turning halfway though, until deeply browned, 3–4 minutes. Transfer to plate with sausage; season with salt.

Add remaining 3 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil to pan. Add 6 garlic cloves, thinly sliced, ½ tsp. freshly ground pepper, ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and reserved squash. Cook, scraping up browned bits and smashing squash with spoon to break up, until lightly browned and broken up into a chunky paste (pieces do not need to be even), about 5 minutes.

Meanwhile, return cooking liquid in reserved pot to a boil over high heat. Cook 12 oz. short tube pasta (such as rigatoni) until very al dente, about 3 minutes less than package directions (it will finish cooking in sauce). Drain, reserving 3 cups pasta cooking liquid.

Add 1 cup pasta cooking liquid to squash and break up squash with spoon until a saucy consistency. Add pasta, another 1 cup pasta cooking liquid, and reserved sausage and dates. Increase heat to medium-high; cook, adding more pasta cooking liquid as needed, until pasta is al dente and coated in sauce, 2–3 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in 1 Tbsp. sherry vinegar or balsamic vinegar. Taste pasta and add more vinegar, salt and/or pepper if needed.

#6806. The 10 Best Lipsticks for Women Over 40 That Deliver Instant Hydration and Lasting Color

Every product on this page was chosen by a Harper's BAZAAR editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

A swipe of lipstick is one of the easiest ways to look instantly put together with minimal effort. Even if you have nothing else on your face, a hint of lip color can lift your complexion. It also works as an accessory or finishing touch for even the simplest outfits.

As we get older, lips naturally feel drier and lose volume. A good balm nourishes and comforts parched lips, but if you want more pigment, many lipsticks are designed for mature skin.

First, steer clear of ultra-matte formulas, as they tend to dehydrate lips and highlight every fine lip line imaginable. They also tend to look flat.

For extra long wear, try a velvety, soft-matte formula instead. It delivers a similar, statement-making finish that's elegant while creating a pillowy, plush effect.

Satin formulas perform well, too. The gentle shine creates the illusion of healthier-looking lips, and it feels less drying throughout the day. That said, brighter shades like reds and oranges can be a little messy to apply, so apply one layer, blend with a fingertip, and blot with a tissue. Repeat to build intensity. If feathering (when the color "bleeds" into fine lines around your lips) is an issue, a clear lip liner around the perimeter should create a barrier.

It's always best to get your skincare benefits from your lip balm, but nourishing plant oils and hydrating ingredients such as glycerin and hyaluronic acid in your lipstick will help maintain hydration as the day goes on.

For makeup artist and Jones Road founder Bobbi Brown, there are no hard-and-fast rules—no matter your age. "It's about your style, what you feel most comfortable in," she tells Bazaar UK.

If you're keen on neutral tones, remember that neutral doesn't mean beige. "Pay attention to what your natural lip color is. I have a slightly bluish-purple tone to my lips. You might have more of a pink tone. It's really great to find a lipstick that really looks like your lips, and the only way is to test it on your bottom lip," says Brown, who notes that a great neutral should not wash you out.

Revered makeup artist Bobbi Brown is no stranger to creating iconic lipsticks. The Classic Lip has all the hallmarks of a modern formula: creamy, intensely hydrating, and richly pigmented. The 12-color range offers enough variety without overwhelming consumers. Expect skin-enhancing neutrals and bolder tones for any occasion.

Trinny London excels at makeup for mature skin, and this recent launch is certainly no exception. It's a glossy, mega-hydrating formula that reflects light beautifully, making lips look plumper, and it's formulated with peptides to help reduce fine lines over time. There's a full spectrum of nude shades, but we love the bold red Poppy for festive nights.

A richly pigmented, buttery-smooth formula that promises to minimize dryness without sacrificing impact. It contains plenty of nourishing oils to keep moisture lasting without feathering into fine lines. It has a rosy scent, so keep that in mind if you're sensitive to fragrance.

Everything Victoria Beckham does delivers instant polish to the lips without extra effort. This slimline lipstick is no exception. It glides on like a tinted lip balm, adding a touch more color while infusing skin with hydration. VB has perfected the art of neutrals, so expect to find easy-to-wear hues for all skin tones. Glide on, then pat to blend any hard edges. It's one of those formulas you won't need a mirror to apply.

Refillable makeup isn't new, but Lisa Eldridge has painstakingly ensured every part of her Rouge Experience lipstick is recyclable, while it still looks like it belongs on a movie star's dresser. The lipstick formula combines oil, gel, and cream to ensure all-day comfort. The color pigments build easily and sit between a soft matte and a shiny finish. It's unfragranced, too.

Creative and image director of Christian Dior Makeup, Peter Philips, reviewed Dior's bestselling lip colors worldwide to create a tightly curated collection of 10 sophisticated, wearable shades for every skin tone. Nude doesn't mean beige, according to Philips, and this line includes a complexion-lifting neutral, whatever that looks like to you. The emollient formula glides on like balmy, satin lipstick but won't budge once it sets. Expect long-wear color without the drying side effects.

When Hourglass creates matte lipsticks, rest assured they feature elevated colors and sit beautifully on the lips without highlighting fine lines, feathering, or flaking. This elegant formula feels velvety soft, with buildable pigments that stay put.

Sisley's interpretation of a shimmery, luminous lip color is as elevated as you've come to expect from this storied French brand. Phyto Rouge Shine is infused with the finest pearlescent particles in a translucent base, delivering sheer, buildable color and a plumping effect that still looks understated and grown-up.

Hermès Beauty creative director Gregoris Pyrpylis drew inspiration from Hermès scarves when designing this collection. This translates into buildable, luminous color and a smooth, tactile finish that feels like a second skin. Even the deepest shades look refined, with a radiance that brightens the face. Plus, the wide, angled bullet makes application as easy as wearing a lip balm.

Not all liquid lipsticks are created equal. Violette's soft, whipped texture is truly modern, delivering intense colors without a heavy feel. The gel-cream texture blurs out fine lines, too, so lips appear plush and smooth.

#6798. Creamy Miso Mushroom Pasta

Mushroom fans: Bookmark this recipe immediately. It will give you everything you want when you crave a creamy mushroom pasta as soon as the crisp fall air sets in. The hardworking trio of miso, Parmesan, and touch of soy sauce delivers an umami bomb of flavor that doesn’t overwhelm, but magnifies, the best of earthy mushrooms. Coupled with luscious noodles enrobed in a creamy (but not heavy) sauce, what’s not to love?

A few helpful notes for pasta success: (1) While any pasta will work, egg-based noodles, like the fettuccine I recommend here, are the best complement to the sauce. The nests (Rummo and De Cecco are great accessible brands) cook far faster than standard straight pasta, almost as fast as fresh. (2) Don’t be afraid to season your mushrooms! Yes, I know this goes against all that we’ve learned about salting them too early in the cooking process, but just a bit of salt will get them going and releasing their water faster for eventual crisp-browned edges. Don’t be alarmed if you see a pool of water at the start of the mushroom cooking—that’s to be expected and just keep going until it evaporates. (3) Don’t forget to reserve plenty of pasta cooking liquid, which is critical to the eventual sauce’s success. I prefer transferring the al dente noodles from the pasta pot to the skillet, letting any residual water come with it (and to ensure you don’t accidentally drain away that liquid gold).

Find more fall favorite meals here: Weeknight Pumpkin Chili; Cream-ish of Mushroom Soup; Mushrooms au Poivre.

Cook 12 oz. egg-based pasta (such as fettuccine nests) in a large pot of boiling salted water, stirring occasionally, until al dente, about 1 minute less than package directions.

Meanwhile, heat 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a large skillet over high. Add 1 lb. crimini or mixed mushrooms (such as button, maitake, oyster, and/or shiitake), sliced ¼" thick or torn into bite-size pieces, and ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt and toss to coat evenly. Spread out into an even layer and cook, undisturbed, until mushrooms are starting to release their liquid, 2–3 minutes (do not be alarmed; there will be a lot). Continue to cook, tossing occasionally, until moisture is almost completely evaporated and edges of mushrooms are starting to brown, 6–8 minutes.

Reduce heat to medium-high; add 5 garlic cloves, thinly sliced, and remaining 1 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil. Cook, tossing often, until garlic is fragrant and golden, 1–2 minutes. Pour in ¾ cup dry white wine, scraping up any browned bits stuck to bottom of pan with a sturdy spatula or flat-edged wooden spoon, and cook until wine is mostly evaporated (you should have about 1 Tbsp. liquid left in pan), about 4 minutes. Reduce heat to medium-low. Add 4 Tbsp. unsalted butter, cut into pieces, and 2 Tbsp. white miso and stir until melted and combined. Slowly pour in ½ cup heavy cream, scraping up any browned bits stuck to bottom of pan; simmer until thickened slightly, 2–3 minutes. Add 1 Tbsp. low-sodium soy sauce; season with freshly ground pepper. Taste and add more salt if needed.

Using tongs, transfer pasta to mushroom mixture and add 1 cup pasta cooking liquid. Increase heat to medium and bring to a simmer. Cook, tossing constantly and adding ½–1 cup more pasta cooking liquid to reach desired sauce consistency if needed, until pasta is al dente and liquid has thickened slightly, about 3 minutes.

Remove pan from heat. Add 1 oz. Parmesan, finely grated (about ½ cup) to pasta and toss to combine. Season generously with more pepper; taste and season with more salt if needed.

Divide pasta among shallow bowls and top with more Parmesan and pepper.

#6795. A Complete Timeline of Justin and Hailey Bieber’s Relationship

The singer and supermodel-turned-skin care mogul are one of Hollywood’s leading power couples.

Justin Bieber and Hailey Baldwin dated on and off long before they became husband and wife. Hailey first met Justin in the late aughts, and they eventually struck up a casual romance.

Though they decided to keep it out of the public eye, this didn’t stop fans from obsessing over their relationship. After a breakup and surprise reconciliation-turned-whirlwind engagement two years later, Justin officially made Hailey his Mrs. during a September 2018 New York City courthouse ceremony. They got married in front of friends and family in a more formal wedding a year later. In May 2024, they announced they were expecting their first child. They welcomed their son, Jack, in August 2024.

From their highly publicized South Carolina nuptials to their adjustment to parenthood, here’s the couple’s full history and how their relationship has evolved.

Hailey has her father, Stephen, to thank for introducing her to her future husband. There’s even footage of their first meeting, which took place backstage at The Today Show. Hailey and Justin—then in their teens—shared a brief handshake and the rest, as they say, is history.

Chaperoned by her father yet again, Hailey attended the New York City premiere of Justin’s documentary Never Say Never. Later that month, Justin confirmed his relationship with Selena Gomez when the couple made their red carpet debut at Vanity Fair’s Oscar After Party.

Hailey officially declared herself a member of the Jelena fan club. The model took to Twitter, sharing her support for the couple. “I don’t care what anyone says but Justin Bieber and Selena Gomez together is the definition of a teenage dream! #word,” Hailey wrote.

After calling it quits with Gomez, Justin was photographed attending church services at Hillsong alongside Hailey and fellow supermodel Kendall Jenner. It wasn’t long before fans began speculating that Hailey and Justin were an item.

Hailey denied any romantic connection between her and Justin. She set the record straight during an interview with E!. “I’ve known [Justin] since I was like 13—and we’ve just been good friends over the years,” Hailey said. “We have just stayed close, and there’s nothing more to it than that.”

Justin backed up Hailey’s statement in an Instagram post. The singer shared a snap of himself and Hailey, writing, “I’m super single and this is my good friend u would know otherwise.”

Hailey joined Justin and his family on vacation in Anguilla, fueling rumors that their friendship was actually something more.

Justin made his romance with Hailey Instagram official. Shortly after New Year’s Day, he shared a photo of them kissing.

Hailey and Justin revealed that their relationship was casual. “We are not an exclusive couple,” Hailey told E!. Meanwhile, in an interview with GQ, Justin called Hailey “someone I really love,” but he added that he didn’t “want to be held down by anything.”

Hailey and Justin ended their brief fling. According to People, Justin also unfollowed Hailey on Instagram amid his new relationship with Sofia Richie.

Following their split, Hailey and Justin completely lost touch for almost two years. In 2020, Hailey shared her thoughts on their time apart: “Our lives seemed to be going in very different directions,” she told ELLE. “I actually think—now that I look back at it being married—that it was a good thing for the two of us, very healthy.”

During Justin and Hailey’s rift, the singer rekindled his romance with Gomez in November 2017. However, by March 2018, Jelena was over for good.

Hailey revealed that she was speaking to Justin again. “We went through a long period of time when we weren’t friends,” she told The Times U.K.. “We’ve moved past that.”

Justin and Hailey appeared as if they were back together. After sharing some PDA at a religious conference, they were spotted together at LIV nightclub in Miami. Just days later, they were photographed holding hands and kissing in New York City.

After rumors of the couple’s engagement began to swirl, Justin confirmed the news on Instagram. He posted two portraits with his new fiancée and penned a lengthy caption devoted to her. “Hailey I am soooo in love with everything about you,” he wrote. “So committed to spending my life getting to know every single part of you.”

Hailey joined the love fest, tweeting, “Not sure what I did in life to deserve such happiness but I am so utterly grateful to God for giving me such an incredible person to share my life with!”

Just two months after their engagement, TMZ ran photographs of the couple walking into New York City’s Marriage Bureau. The next day, People claimed that Hailey and Justin obtained their marriage license, officially making them husband and wife.

Meanwhile, Hailey dismissed the gossip on Twitter: “I understand where the speculation is coming from, but I’m not married yet!”

The couple finally confirmed their marriage status. Justin shared an Instagram photo of him and Hailey with the caption “My wife is awesome.” The following day, Hailey changed her last name to Bieber on all of her social media accounts.

TMZ broke the news that a second wedding was imminent after the date was moved several times. The outlet acquired a photo of a save the date card, which revealed that the ceremony would take place on September 30 in South Carolina.

Mr. and Mrs. Bieber officially tied the knot…again! People disclosed the details of their ceremony, which took place at Somerset Chapel in Bluffton, South Carolina. Vows (and Tiffany & Co. wedding bands) were exchanged “as the sun set.” The star-studded guest list included Kendall Jenner, Camila Morrone, and Jaden Smith, among others.

A day later, Justin basked in wedded bliss as he shared photos from the couple’s reception.

The Biebers continued to share photos from their big day. Hailey put her Off-White by Virgil Abloh wedding dress on full display, including her elaborate train, which read “’till death do us part.” Justin wore a Celine tuxedo.

Weeks later, the newlyweds found themselves embroiled in Jelena fan drama, after Justin’s ex dropped her new single “Lose You To Love Me.” The track captured Gomez’s feelings moving on from her 10-year on-off romance with Justin and closing that chapter.

Shortly after the song came out, Hailey upset some Jelena fans when she posted an Instagram Story, where she shared that she was listening to Summer Walker’s “I’ll Kill You.” Hailey denied that this was a dig at Gomez. Commenting beneath JustJared’s Instagram post, she wrote, “please stop with this nonsense. There is no ‘response.’ This is complete BS.”

Gomez, meanwhile, told her fans on Instagram Live not to attack Hailey. “I am grateful for the response that the song is getting. I’m so grateful,” she said. “However, I do not stand for women tearing women down. And I will never, ever be by that. So please be kind to everyone. It doesn’t matter what the situation is. If you’re my fans, don’t be rude to anybody, please. Don’t go off and say things that you just feel in the moment. And just please, from me, know that that’s not my heart. My heart is only to release things that I feel that are me and that I’m proud of. And that’s all that I’ll say, yeah.”

Hailey tried to shut down feud rumors herself when she liked Gomez’s Instagram post promoting “Lose You To Love Me.” A source close to the Biebers also assured E! that things were copacetic. “It isn’t ideal for Hailey,” the insider told the outlet, “but she understands the creative process of writing music and that Justin had a past. Justin and Hailey both want Selena to be happy and in a good place and aren’t fazed by it.”

Justin rang in the decade with his new single “Yummy,” which details his sex life with Hailey.

Hailey landed the March 2020 cover of ELLE. She spoke candidly about the couple’s decision to delay their South Carolina ceremony for a year. “When we first got married, we were just figuring out our life together,” she said. “I felt like putting a wedding in the middle of all of that would be really hectic and stressful.”

Although the Biebers weren’t ready for children yet, Hailey was already thinking about parenting. Amid worldwide protests in solidarity with Black Lives Matter, Hailey discussed her outlook on motherhood. Regarding her future children, she told Vogue India, “They will be raised knowing how to treat people, why we don’t say certain things, and why we respect and acknowledge and give credit where credit is due.”

The Biebers attended their first Met Gala as husband and wife. Hailey stunned in a Saint Laurent column gown and matching wayfarer sunglasses. Justin paired his sleek suit with customized Nike sneakers.

Hailey and Justin appeared on the In Good Faith with Chelsea & Judah Smith podcast, where they discussed the challenges they faced in their first year of marriage. At the time, Justin was battling with severe bouts of depression. Hailey admitted that watching her partner struggle wasn’t easy.

“There were days where I literally was like, ‘I don’t know if he’s going to be okay.’ Something really deep down inside of me was like, ‘He’s going to get through it.’ I just didn’t know how long it was going to take. That’s what I think was the hardest thing. There’s no guarantees,” she said.

Nevertheless, Hailey was determined to stick by her husband: “Imagine abandoning somebody in the middle of the worst time of their life, potentially. I’m not that type of person,” she said.

Amid the launch of her skin care line Rhode, Hailey did an interview with WSJ Magazine. The entrepreneur shared her thoughts on having children. “I think ideally in the next couple of years we would try. But there’s a reason they call it try, right?” she said. “You don’t know how long that process is ever going to take. Definitely no kids this year; that would be a little bit hectic, I think.”

Hailey also revealed her decision to stop discussing her marriage in interviews. “It doesn’t feel worth it to me anymore,” she explained. “I try to have an open conversation with someone, and then it gets taken out of context.”

Hailey was hospitalized after having stroke-like symptoms, though she fortunately fully recovered. Her health scare left Justin reasonably shaken, with a source close to the couple telling People, “[He] is probably more traumatized than even she is. When it happened, there was a lot of panic. Justin later discussed the situation during one of his concerts. “You know, it’s kind of crazy how life throws you curveballs,” he said during a Denver performance. “Most of you probably know or seen the news about my wife …but she’s okay, she’s good, she’s strong. It’s been really scary. But I know for a fact that God has her in the palms of his hands, and that’s a good thing.”

Hailey accompanied her husband at the Grammys. She opted for a flowy strapless gown, which led some fans to speculate that she was hiding a growing baby bump. Just months after Hailey’s hospitalization, Justin had a health scare of his own. A virus called Ramsay Hunt syndrome left half of the singer’s face paralyzed, but he eventually recovered. A source told People that although this year has been “overwhelming” for the couple, relationship-wise, “they’re unbreakable.”

During an interview with Good Morning America, Hailey shared a promising update on her husband’s health. “He is getting better every single day. He’s feeling a lot better and, obviously, it was just a very scary and random situation to happen, but he’s going to be totally okay, and I’m just grateful that he’s fine,” she said.

Ahead of the couple’s fourth anniversary, Hailey discussed her relationship with Justin in Harper’s Bazaar. “[Justin’s] still the person that I wanna be rushing back to,” she said. “I might fly somewhere and go do a job, but I can’t wait to come back and hang out. Hailey appeared on the Call Her Daddy podcast. Hailey went on to discuss her seemingly speedy engagement to Justin, which took place just two months after they began dating again. “I’m like, ‘yeah, that seemed really drastic and really crazy,’” she said. “But that was what we felt was a decision between the two of us, and it felt correct for the two of us at the time, and clearly, we were right because here we are, four years later.”

Hailey and Gomez posed for pictures together at the Academy Museum Gala, proving once and for all that there is no drama between them. Justin also shared a photo of him with Hailey in a photo booth.

Hailey was dressed as Kim and Justin was her friend, Ron. Baby Jack was dressed in a pink onesie as Ron’s pet naked mole rat, Rufus.

Hailey also shared a pic of Jack’s feet in a Nightmare Before Christmas-themed onesie.

On Friday, November 29, Hailey posted a photo carousel on Instagram including a candid family pic of herself, Justin, and Jack. In the photo, the group is bundled up for an outdoor walk, with Justin in a gray and black camo fleece and matching jacket, Hailey in a fuzzy coat, and Jack in a gray hoodie lined with white shearling.

She captioned the carousel, “November aka the best month of the year.”

On December 16, Justin shared photos from a trip the couple took. In one shot, Hailey appears kissing his cheek, while he returns the favor in another pic. “💕🙈😛🫶🏼,” he captioned one post on Instagram.

On January 1, Justin signaled his marriage with Hailey is going just fine on his Instagram Story. He shared a shot of her in a two-piece set and wrote, “Um goin anywhere with u bb. Happy new year.”

On January 21, Justin drew attention for briefly unfollowing Hailey on Instagram. He followed her again and posted an explanation on his Instagram Story. “Someone went on my account and unfollowed my wife,” he wrote. “Shit is getting suss out here.”

In the hours following, both Hailey and Justin shared new photos of each other on Instagram. Hailey tucked in a shot of Justin sleeping to a carousel of photos she posted.

On Valentine’s Day, the couple seemingly offered updates on their relationship with some funny Instagram posts. Hailey first shared a picture in her Stories indicating she may be “mad” at her husband at the moment, but that doesn’t keep her away from him. The Story included a picture of the animated cat Topsy from Tom & Jerry stomping across the room, with a caption that read, “When you’re mad at him, and he says ‘come here, baby.’”

She added some heart-themed emojis to make the message even sweeter.

The singer shared a number of photos to celebrate Hailey on Valentine’s Day, too, first with a carousel of pics he captioned, “HAPPY VALENTINES DAY FROM THE BIEBERS.”

She shared one of those pics in her own Instagram Stories, writing, “My best friend is my Valentine.”

Justin then shared a couple more photos with a kiss emoji in which Hailey can be seen holding his hand and looking over his shoulder. She wore a fluffy black jacket and cropped top that showed off her toned midriff. He wore a leopard print tie.

They were later seen arriving at the iconic Beverly Hills Hotel for a Valentine’s Day meal, with Justin wearing a black puffer jacket over a gray hoodie, wide-legged jeans in photos taken while they were greeted outside.

For his 31st birthday, Justin shared a carousel of photos from the celebration that included a rare picture of baby Jack.

The model shared a few more photos with her husband in her Stories for his birthday, one in black-and-white in which she is lying in his arms on the floor. Over it, she wrote, “Happy birthday to my love.”

Justin and Hailey made an appearance together on May 18, attending game 7 of the Toronto Maple Leafs’ playoff series against the Florida Panthers. Sitting rinkside at Scotiabank Arena in Toronto, the couple appeared in good spirits throughout the night. Hailey wore a blue Leafs jacket to support Justin’s longtime favorite team, while Justin shared multiple Instagram posts and Stories from the outing. They included backstage shots, rinkside selfies, and a series of PDA-filled photos.

“Made it into the building,” he captioned one post of Hailey walking ahead of him as they arrived.

In another, he expressed his optimism for the team despite their loss that evening. He wrote, “I don’t remember a time in my life when I haven’t been obsessed with the leafsssss. This year we made it farther than we have in so long and I’m happy about that. I can be patient ’cuz I know this is the team to do it.”

That same month, Hailey addressed how her marriage is perceived in a Vogue interview, saying, “I feel like I’ve fought so hard to try to get people to understand me, or know who I am, or see me for me. And people just don’t want to sometimes. And there’s nothing you can do about that. I’ve been in a position where I’ve tried to tell my side of a story or correct a narrative or tell the truth of a lie and then they go, Well, she’s lying. Imagine how trapping that feels.”

She added, “I’ve learned so much from Justin, really. He’s been doing this literally since he was a child and he has had to face the most scrutiny of any person that I know. He was like, ‘Baby, trust me, I’ve been here before many, many times. You’re not going to win. There is no winning.’”

In June, Hailey drew attention when she was photographed without her wedding ring on two outings in New York City, but was then seen wearing her ring again, including the upgraded engagement ring she debuted last year.

A source speaking to Entertainment Tonight explained the current state of the couple’s marriage: “Justin and Hailey have been struggling in their relationship,” the insider said. “They both want to salvage their marriage, but right now things are not good.” The source added that their friends believe they can work things out, too.

There are issues on both sides, the source detailed: “Justin has been getting irritated easily and feels like Hailey can be superficial about the way their relationship looks in the public eye, and Justin’s lack of motivation has been upsetting for her.”

On July 14, Justin shared shots from a recent trip to Italy with his wife.

On July 16, he shared a carousel of pics from another recent vacation, opening with a shot of him giving her a kiss on the cheek.

On July 17, a source told Entertainment Tonight that things have improved, but the couple never considered calling it quits, due to their deep love for each other and their son, nearly 1-year-old Jack.

“Justin and Hailey are doing much better these days, [but] things were up and down for a bit,” the source said. “Even though they have gone through rough patches in their marriage, divorce was not on the table. Hailey loves Justin and the family they’ve built.”

The couple appeared to be having a fun time after a listening party for Justin’s new album, Swag, on July 25. They both shared photos of a hot kiss and Justin shared a number of images from his big event.

Justin discussed his issues with Hailey on his album Swag and in “Daisies” and

In the “Walking Away” chorus, he sang, “Baby, I ain’t walking away / You were my diamond / Gave you a ring/ I made you a promise / I told you I’d change / It’s just human nature / These growing pains / And baby, I ain’t walking away.”

The couple was seen on a date night at Giorgio Baldi in Santa Monica dressed up for their evening out. The model was wearing a black minidress with ruched fabric forming long sleeves and a collared neckline, plunging down in the middle. Hailey wore the dress with black pointed-toe heels and carried a black handbag. She left her hair down and wore small silver earrings and sunglasses.

Justin wore an oversized black leather coat over a bright blue hoodie and wide-legged jeans, as well as a SKYLRK white beanie and sunglasses. Justin held the car door open for his wife before following her into the eatery.

On September 5, Justin dropped Swag II, the surprise follow-up to his July album, and Hailey was quick to show her support. She celebrated the album’s release on her Instagram Stories with a “Happy swag II day” post and highlighted tracks like “Bad Honey,” “Love Song,” “I Do,” and “When It’s Over.”

The record itself features multiple references to Hailey and their son, Jack. In “I Do,” Justin echoes his wedding vows, singing that she’ll “always be the one that I choose,” while “Mother in You” reflects on the parts of Hailey he sees in their child. Other songs, including “I Think You’re Special,” “Love Song,” and “Safe Space,” emphasize his devotion to her and the life they’ve built together, even as he nods to past challenges in their marriage.

On September 13, they celebrated their seventh wedding anniversary, and a source spoke to People about the current status of their relationship four days later. “They’ve had challenges like anyone else, but they always come back to the same thing: They truly believe they are soulmates,” the insider said. “Becoming parents has only deepened their bond. Jack is the center of everything for them.”

Justin and Hailey are also both “thriving right now.” The source added, “They just celebrated their wedding anniversary, he’s on top of the charts, and she’s breaking records in beauty. They are both very focused. Justin’s super grateful for his fans. He’s hyped about Coachella. Hailey will be there of course.”

On Friday, October 25, Justin shared some pictures with Hailey following his SKYLRK basketball team’s The League game. In the photos, she is sitting in his lap and giving him a hug as they’re surrounded by people, smiling broadly.

The next day, Pop Base shared a video of the couple at a Dijon concert in San Diego. In the short clip, Justin is standing behind his wife with his arms around her. She leans back against him and they sway to the music. At one point, he gently strokes a strand of her hair. Their friend, Kendall Jenner, can be seen beside them enjoying the show as well.

Justin and Hailey shared photos from their family Halloween celebration on November 1. The family dressed as characters from The Incredibles, with Hailey as Elastigirl, Justin as Mr. Incredible, and their son, Jack, as Jack-Jack.

On November 5, Justin posted a photo from Kendall Jenner’s 30th birthday celebration showing Hailey kissing him at the private beachside party. He wore a white tank top and tan pants, while Hailey appeared in a leopard-print minidress.

Hailey and Justin spoke about Jack during a Twitch stream on November 12. Hailey described his personality, saying, “He’s like that. He’ll just walk up and start hugging.” Justin added, “I always wanted a kid who wasn’t, like, super shy, and didn’t want to go to people. He’s super personable and open. It’s too cute.”

On December 21, Hailey and Justin were photographed out in West Hollywood. Justin wore black-and-white shorts, a gray hoodie, and sneakers, while Hailey paired an ivory top and charcoal pants with a long black coat.

Justin posted a selfie with Hailey to celebrate Christmas on December 25. In the photo, the couple embraced in winter outfits. He captioned it, “MERRY CHRISTMAS FROM THE BIEBERS 🫂🎅❤️”

On January 16, Hailey participated in a viral 2016 Instagram trend and included a throwback photo of herself and Justin kissing. She captioned the post, “you just had to be there.”

On February 18, Hailey shared a new update about motherhood during her appearance on Jake Shane’s Therapuss podcast. She revealed their son, Jack, had started singing along to one of Justin’s early hits. “He does [listen to Justin’s music]. He’s been saying, ‘Baby, oh, baby, oh, baby, oh’,” she said, adding that it began “literally in the last two days.”

Hailey also spoke about her desire to grow their family in the future. “I definitely do want one more [kid],” she said, adding, “I’m not in a rush, but I definitely want one more. Maybe I’ll have four more. Maybe I’ll have three. I don’t know, I really don’t know. I’m just taking it one day at a time.”

Hailey supported Justin during his Coachella headlining performance, attending the show. During one moment in his set, Justin gave a shout-out to his family while singing, “Mom and Dad, hallelujah. Hailey babe, hallelujah. Baby Jack, hallelujah.” The camera then cut to Hailey in the audience, and she blew him a kiss and waved to the crowd.

On April 14, Hailey spoke about her marriage and family life with Justin in her Interview magazine cover profile. Discussing their personal style, she said, “We both just really like expressing ourselves through our style and supporting each other’s individualism.” She added, “On a day-to-day basis I’m like, ‘I don’t give a shit what you want to wear. Are you comfortable? Do you feel good?’ That’s all that matters to me.”

Hailey also shared insight into dressing their son, Jack Blues, saying, “My vibe with him is cozy and yummy and cute and simple.”

Reflecting on motherhood, she said the most exciting part is “just seeing this little human evolve before your eyes. They grow so fast and they change so much and there’s always so much excitement. You’re watching them experience life for the first time, so you kind of feel like you’re experiencing it that way with them.”

Later that month, on April 28, Justin posted a photo of himself and Hailey from Coachella. Hailey wore a blue athletic jacket with coordinating shorts and carried a black shoulder bag, while Justin paired a washed charcoal hoodie with black pants and a bright pink knit cap. He captioned the post, “😍.”

On May 10, Hailey celebrated Mother’s Day by sharing a black-and-white selfie with Jack on her Instagram Story. “I love being your mommy,” she wrote alongside the photo.

On May 29, Justin posted a carousel of photos from what looks like a fun getaway with Hailey and Jack. He started it with photo booth images of himself and his wife, and added a few pictures with Jack at what looks like a goat farm.

Just ahead of his performance at the World Cup finals, Justin and Hailey attended Fanatics Fest together in New York City. Afterwards, Justin shared a number of carousels on his Instagram timeline featuring his wife that were seemingly taken at the event.

Justin shared another glimpse of his summer with Hailey on Instagram. In one photo, the couple sat together at a Los Angeles Dodgers game, where Hailey kissed Justin while holding his face. She wore a white T-shirt, black sunglasses, and a navy baseball cap, while Justin wore a graphic T-shirt with wired earbuds around his neck.

The carousel also included other photos from the game, a look at several pairs of Skylrk sneakers, and a close-up of Justin cuddling their son, Jack Blues.

Justin captioned the post simply, “❤️❤️❤️.”

Hailey and Justin attended Finneas O’Connell and Claudia Sulewski’s wedding at San Ysidro Ranch in Montecito, California.

For the outdoor ceremony, Hailey wore a bright green archival Versace halter dress with a plunging neckline and gathered detailing through the bodice. She accessorized with pearl earrings and carried a coordinating handbag. Her hair was swept into a sleek updo.

Justin went classic in a black suit with a white dress shirt and black tie, finishing his look with sunglasses. The couple was photographed mingling with fellow guests during the celebration.

Hailey and Justin appeared together on the cover of the inaugural issue of WYouth, where they answered a series of questions about their personal preferences. While the couple differed on everything from their favorite cities (New York for Hailey and Los Angeles for Justin) to their go-to karaoke songs (“Bohemian Rhapsody” for Hailey and Chris Brown’s “With You” for Justin), both named the spa as their favorite way to unwind.

Justin marked the couple’s eighth wedding anniversary with an Instagram carousel of the two playing pool. In one of the photos, the pair leaned in toward each other for a kiss.

“8 years until infinity ❤️ NEW BEGINNINGS ♾️ I love you baby Happy Anniversary,” he wrote in the caption.

Hailey and Justin celebrated Halloween with an angel and devil couples costume, which the singer showcased in Instagram photos taken by photographer Amber Asaly.

Hailey styled a white blazer and feather-trimmed bra with black micro shorts and embellished peep-toe heels. She completed her costume with feathered wings and a white halo. Justin opted for a monochromatic red ensemble featuring a loose-fitting jacket, matching pants, narrow sunglasses, and a horned headpiece.

Two days after turning 30, Hailey shared photos on Instagram from her birthday trip to the Bahamas. The carousel included two sweet shots of the couple, including one of them kissing.

#6792. 7 Sneaker Outfits That Put a Fresh Spin on Your Favorite Kicks

Every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

I’m what you might call a sneaker hoarder. But after building a capsule wardrobe I currently swear by, I’ve found that three pairs have become the foundation of most of my fall outfits: my black Adidas Superstars, which tap into the retro sneaker revival and rising noir sneaker trend I’m loving lately; my earth-toned Salomon XT-Whispers, perfect for an easy gorpcore moment; and my lilac Adidas x Wales Bonner Japan shoes, which add a subtle splash of color to neutral looks while complementing the rich hues in my autumn lineup. With those themes in mind, and inspired by some of this year’s most viral celebrity getups and standout street-style looks, I’ve gathered a quick guide to seven exciting sneaker outfits below.

Maybe you’re eager to invest in a new staple pair, or maybe you already have one of these favorites tucked away at the back of your closet. Either way, there’s plenty of fresh inspiration to copy and paste this season. Ahead, discover key pairs to shop (if you don’t already own them) and the chic pieces to wear with them.

Y2K icons like Vans and Converse are quietly making a comeback, stylishly co-signed by stars like Bella Hadid and Margot Robbie. Here, Robbie nails the cold-weather off-duty formula, swapping classic booties for black All Star high-tops to give her cozy gray polo, leather trench, and straight-leg jeans a more casual edge. A zesty red beanie completes the look, breaking up the muted tones.

By Anthropologie 100 Percent Brushed Cashmere Beanie

Even a few years after Adidas Sambas surged in popularity, the legendary indoor soccer-inspired shoe has cemented its status as a bona fide modern classic. Zoë Kravitz was recently spotted wearing a black-and-white pair while filming her new rom-com, Die Alive, in New York, styling them with flowy black trousers and a burgundy sweater and scarf. It’s a polished yet easygoing ensemble perfect for everything from bakery runs to overdue weekend catch-ups.

Saks Basic Cashmere Easy Crewneck Sweater

Hollister High-Rise Pleated Wide-Leg Pants

Or, as aforementioned, try switching up a neutral outfit with a colorful pair of kicks. As Jennifer Lawrence shows, an emerald- or forest-green sneaker feels just right for fall and winter, easily styled back to baggy jeans, a chunky turtleneck, and a navy coat.

The coolest outfits often hinge on contrast, mixing different textures, proportions, and aesthetics. This Paris Fashion Week showgoer went polished on top with a striped button-down and plaid blazer (also creating a nice pattern play) and sporty on bottom with classic track pants and chunky black Asics sneakers. An oversized denim tote introduces yet another interesting element.

Favorite Daughter The Dean Plaid Notch Lapel Blazer

Speaking of contrast, I love the idea of using a chunky sneaker to give tailored separates a cool, nonchalant feel. A relaxed-fit tuxedo blazer and drapey wide-leg trousers are a match made in street-style heaven when teamed with a boxy white tee and metallic trainers, like the celebrity-favorite New Balance 530s.

Banana Republic Factory Double Breasted Tuxedo Blazer

Lauren Ralph Lauren Pleated Stretch Jersey Wide-Leg Pant

PerfectWhiteTee Harley Cotton Boxy Crew Tee

Retro runner silhouettes, with their slim, streamlined uppers and slightly thicker soles, are another IYKYK trend to keep on your radar. Taking a cue from this Paris Fashion Week attendee, don’t be afraid to work traditionally spring-ready colors into your look: a baby-blue cable-knit sweater and soft yellow track jacket look lovely—and still feel relevant—alongside a chocolate-brown maxi skirt, matching sneakers, and a rich burgundy handbag.

Vineyard Vines Cashmere Cable Crewneck Sweater

Just like a go-to pair of low-profile kicks, a good ol’ graphic tee can be styled with just about anything in your closet—and it’s the kind of playful, sentimental piece that’ll spark joy every time you reach for it. For a unique combo, pair your favorite artist tee with sporty pieces like a nylon skirt and track jacket. An oversized briefcase-style bag adds a sleek touch.

#6791. How Nara Smith Crafted Her Style From Scratch

The model-slash-chef joined Harper’s Bazaar’s The Good Buy podcast to discuss styling herself for videos, the vegetable jacket she has her eye on, and the pieces she steals from her husband

The Good Buy is a podcast from Harper’s Bazaar in which editors Leah Chernikoff and Lynette Nylander invite celebrities, designers, models, and tastemakers to talk shop: what they buy, where they got it, and why it matters. Come down the fashion rabbit hole and take a peek inside the closets and shopping carts of the world’s most stylish people. Learn how they use style to tell their stories.

It’s been three years since Nara Smith first burst onto the scene, carving out her own niche of CookTok with her highly stylized “from scratch” videos, in which she makes home-cooked versions of everyday food for her family. Narrating her process in a soft ASMR voice, she’s crafted everything from Skittles and Starbursts to chili soup and cornbread, with easy-to-follow (yet labor-intensive) recipes now immortalized in her debut cookbook, Homemade. Always dolled up and dressed in an archival ensemble or a look pulled straight off the runway, she’s blurred the lines between food and fashion—and managed to make spending a full day in the kitchen look utterly glamorous.

Smith has translated this signature formula into brand deals and partnerships, “cooking” Marc Jacobs totes and sunscreen bottles from scratch. She’s sat front row at Fashion Week, embarked on a cookbook press tour dressed in Schiaparelli vegetable prints, and starred in Skims campaigns alongside her model husband, Lucky Blue.

She’s a chef, a writer, a model, and a mother—but if there’s one title she wholeheartedly rejects, it’s that of a trad wife. “That’s one of the narratives that I have a really hard time wrapping my head around,” she told Harper’s Bazaar. “You don’t see me getting on a plane, hopping to New York, modeling, coming back—all while I have a newborn—paying bills, filming content, getting my kids dressed. Being put into a certain box, just because people think that I’m slaving away, is so weird to me. I’m a working mom who gets to go about her day in a very different way than [someone with] a normal nine-to-five job would.”

“I love dressing up. I love fashion so much,” she continued. “Sometimes my outfits aren’t the most practical, but then again fashion isn’t always practical. That’s what I do. I post videos of me cooking for my kids and my husband. It’s really not that deep.”

Now, the star joins Harper’s Bazaar’s The Good Buy to dive into where she shops, the designers catching her eye, and how she styles herself for video shoots.

“It’s my Super Bowl. It’s so fun seeing what brands send down the runway, it’s nice to see trends, it’s nice to see what everyone’s gravitating towards—but it’s also so nice catching up with friends. I’m always like, ‘I don’t know anyone,’ but then I go and I’m like, ‘Hello, hello, let me say hi to that person.’ It’s always really fun, and then I get to dress up. I’m a glam girl, fashion girl, through and through.”

“It was [an IMG Models contest.] I hash-tagged all of my photos and then one day [scout] Jeni Rose reached out to me via DM. And two weeks later, I was in Paris. I don’t know why they said ‘That girl.’ My eyebrows were so thin, I was in the highest heels you could imagine, couldn’t walk in them. I was 14. And they saw something in me that I didn’t at the time.”

“I met my husband and I moved to the States and I couldn’t work because of my visa situation. In that time, we also had two kids. So I was like, ‘Okay, I’ll stay at home with them, you go model.’ So Lucky did what he did, and after a while, I was finding my way back into modeling while also simultaneously starting to post on Instagram and TikTok. I got diagnosed with an autoimmune [disorder] which forced me to cook, and then without knowing I really just blew up and then transitioned into a content creator.

“It’s nice having built a name that is a brand, to where now I get to collaborate with brands. It’s not just me being a model or a mannequin for a brand, where I’m bringing their vision to life. Now it’s a collaboration, because they usually tap into what I have to offer and it feels like I have creative control and I can speak my mind. It feels very warm.”

“I forget [how big the audience is] because to me, it’s my phone and me in the kitchen with my tripod. I don’t have a team, I don’t have people at my house. It’s me styling myself, getting myself ready, doing the recipes, doing all of these things. And then I post it and I go about my day. But then when I leave the house and I get stopped a bunch, I’m like, ‘Oh! People actually watch me.’ And I get so excited.”

“I think about where my counter cuts me, which is around my hips, so I make sure everything hip and up is good. Sometimes the bottom is a little wonky or I’m not wearing a shoe. I feel like tops can get boring, so I try to play with silhouettes and textures or sleeves.

“Sometimes I like to match the color or the texture [to the food]. Sometimes I like to match the time period. I remember I made a milkshake and I was like, ‘When were they really popular? What were they wearing in that era?’ There’s always some element that ties it back to what I’m making.”

“It was a Bottega bag, a big brown woven one. That was my first splurge ever, and I felt sick to my stomach about it for three weeks. I thought about returning it for so long, but I’m glad I didn’t because it fits everything.”

“I don’t think I regret buying anything, because I’m really careful. If it’s not an immediate yes, I will leave the store and think about it for weeks. I remember this vintage Cartier watch that I saw two years ago and I still think about it daily. Maybe in a few years I’m going to get it, but it was just too much money to spend. Maybe when I hit 30.”

“Vintage denim. You can never have enough denim. They come in all washes, all sizes, all cuts—I love a bootcut, I love a flair, I love a straight cut. The possibilities are endless. I have been really lucky where I walk into stores and they look at me and pull me stuff. Ebay is great. Or my husband—sometimes I’ll go onto his side of the closet and I’ll get a pair and take it to the tailor. He’s never gonna know.”

“There’s this Schiaparelli jacket that just walked down the runway; it has vegetables on it. They gave it to me for this press tour, but I want to buy it when it comes out and it’s probably going to cost me an arm and a leg. It feels special. It feels like it’s in my realm. The craftsmanship is insanity, and the color black is so velvety and saturated, it pulls you in. And it fits me like a glove.

“If I do splurge, I want it to be timeless enough. If [my daughter] Rumble sees that in 30 years, she’s going to think that’s the most iconic jacket she will ever see. When there’s an estate sale, when I’ve passed? Do you know how iconic that’s gonna be?”

“I got some Sonny Angels that were really cute—these little figurines with cute heads. Also, my friend Iris [Law], she’s the most whimsical person. We never get time in Paris, but we got time in Paris, and she knows the best [shops]. She took me to this perfume place with the best Parisian perfume that has all these stories. So I kind of went ham and bought a bunch of perfumes. And one of them was a scent that Marilyn Monroe wore.”

#6788. Denmark’s Queen Mary Delivers a Trifecta of Designer Looks During Her Historic State Visit to Colombia

From a D&G pencil skirt to a Saloni maxi dress

Denmark’s Queen Mary is looking posh and joyful on day two of her historic state visit to Colombia—a trip which makes her the first Danish queen to travel to the country.

Today, the monarch was given a tour of the Gold Museum in Bogotá, and later walked through the city’s main square, Plaza de Bolívar, with Mayor Carlos Fernando Galán.

The official visit runs through November 26, and the queen’s agenda includes learning about the country’s post-earthquake reconstruction efforts (three months after a 7.4-magnitude earthquake struck Colombia) and ongoing sustainability projects.

To arrive in the country, Mary went sharp in a black Forte Forte single-breasted blazer with a frilly sky-blue Stenströms Darya blouse, which she paired with black trousers, Malone Souliers Marion 70 pumps, and black Gucci glasses, plus some gold jewelry.

Then, for this afternoon’s engagements, she slipped into a sophisticated business look, the highlight of which was a black-and-white tweed pencil skirt from Dolce & Gabbana and a black collared top from Red Valentino. To round out the ensemble, she reached for sheer black tights, plus matching stilettos and a leather handbag.

The royal performed another quick change for her evening engagement: a reception in the Biodiversario greenhouse at Bogotá’s Botanical Garden. The look was a breezy wine midi dress with a fun dotted print by Saloni. In semi-sheer fabric, it featured a high neck, long sleeves, a cinched waist, and a long skirt that reached her ankles. Black-and-white heels added the perfect contrast to the colorful maxi.

#6787. Cider-Braised Sausage and Lentils

I haven’t made a meal in the French countryside in fall; but sometimes I dream, and these slow-cooked lentils are what I’d make in such a situation. Back in my American reality, it still makes an excellent dinner or hearty weekend lunch. Look for mild smoked Austrian or German sausages, which lean on mellow herbs and warm spices (sometimes, if you’re lucky, they’re also stuffed with a nutty cheese)—this style is already cooked to a safe temperature, but the casing’s texture is greatly improved when seared before reheating. If your shop only carries sweet Italian sausage or something like an apple-stuffed chicken sausage, both work in a pinch. What a treat it will be to actually finish off that gallon of apple cider you impulsively bought last week in the lentil-braising liquid.

More great fall recipes this way: Charred Cabbage With Sausages and Apples; Pork Chops With Green Chiles and Apples; Mustardy Cider-Braised Pork Chops.

Heat 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a large high-sided skillet or a medium heavy pot over medium-high. Cook 6–8 smoked Austrian or German sausages (1–1½ lb.), turning often, until deeply browned on all sides, about 4 minutes. Transfer to a plate.

Combine 1 large red or yellow onion, finely chopped, 3 celery stalks, finely chopped, 1 large carrot, peeled, finely chopped, 1 tsp. freshly ground pepper, and ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and remaining 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in same pan. Reduce heat to medium and cook, stirring often and scraping up any browned bits stuck to bottom of pan, until vegetables are softened, 6–8 minutes. Add 5 garlic cloves, thinly sliced, and cook, stirring, just until fragrant, about 1 minute.

Add 2 cups low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth, 1½ cups apple cider, 1½ cups French green lentils, picked through, rinsed, ½ cup finely chopped parsley, 3 Tbsp. Dijon or whole grain mustard, and remaining ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt to pan. Increase heat to high and bring to a boil. Cook until liquid is slightly reduced, about 5 minutes. Cover pan, reduce heat to medium-low, and cook until lentils are tender and most of the liquid is absorbed but mixture is still saucy, 30–35 minutes.

Uncover pan and stir in 1 Tbsp. apple cider vinegar or red wine vinegar. Nestle sausages into lentil mixture and add any juices pooled on plate. Simmer until sausages are warmed through, about 5 minutes. Top with parsley leaves and reserved celery leaves to serve.

#6780. Before You Shop Glossier’s Black Friday Sale, Here’s Our Ranking of the 15 Best Products

Once the new kid on the block, Glossier is one of the biggest and most well-known (and loved) makeup and skincare brands out there. “Cloud Paint” and “Boy Brow” aren’t just product names now; they’re trends that developed whole product categories, igniting the launch of a zillion dupes. It’s iconic, to say the least.

Glossier became known for its minimalist approach, both in packaging and product formula. Every makeup product is filled with skin-loving ingredients (like hyaluronic acid and glycerin), the skincare is gentle and suitable for all skin types, and their approach to beauty is simple and fresh-faced. From the best-selling Balm Dotcom to makeup artist-favorite Stretch Concealer to the hidden-gem bodycare—choosing a favorite child is hard. That’s why I ranked and reviewed all of the best Glossier products below.

While we’re here... Glossier is running its annual Black Friday sale right now. FWIW, Glossier rarely goes on sale. The brand really only does discounts during its annual Black Friday sale, meaning you won’t see prices this low for likely another year. I know 25% off doesn’t feel all that buzzy or exciting (it’s not the same shock as all those TVs and gaming consoles you stood in line for as a kid), but it’s one of the highest I’ve ever seen Glossier offer. And if you spend more than $100, your discount shoots up to 30% off. That, my friends, is a steal in the Glossier world.

Did you too pluck your eyebrows just a little (read: a lot) when you were younger? Unforch, the sentiment is v relatable, but this brow gel helps give that fluffy appearance even when you don’t have too much going on above your eyelids. “It's the only brow gel that visibly thickens my brows upon application,” editor Corinne Sullivan notes. “My favorite thing is how it keeps my brows conditioned rather than crunchy like other products do.”

When it comes to blush, Glossier’s beginner-friendly Cloud Paint will forever remain a cult-favorite pick among beauty lovers. “Sorry, but Cloud Paint is still the GOAT of all cream blushes,” beauty editor Beth Gillette shares. “Yup, I said it!!! It blends better than any other formula I've used, especially with my fingers, making it practically the simplest blush to apply ever. The shades are timeless and trendy and I'll never get tired of 'em.”

Beauty director Lauren Balsamo is obsessed with these blushes (she even said it was her favorite makeup launch last year). “The original Cloud Paint provides a nice wash of color that lasts for an hour or two, but Plush Blush lasts all day without fading, even on my extremely oily skin,” she says. “I’m not someone who wears primer or sets my makeup with a setting spray, so I fully expect most makeup to fade after a few hours, but Plush Blush survived a 12-hour office day on my cheeks.”

If dewy glasslike skin is what you’re after, dewy glasslike is what you’ll get! As the name suggests, Futuredew is the oil-serum hybrid that will make future you dewy as hell. Packed with nourishing oils and plant-based extracts, you’ll be looking as radiant as ever in no time. Wear it alone, under makeup, or as a highlighter on the high points of your face.

Makeup artist Katie Jane Hughes got me obsessed with this brow pencil, and now it’s virtually the only one I’ll use. It has a unique, straight tip (versus the usual fine, pointy one) that helps create hairlike strokes and fill in my brows with the same tool. My brows look natural and soft every time.

Glossier might not have been the first to launch a lip oil, but it made a pretty damn good one. It makes my lips look plush and glossy and hydrates like a lip treatment. The tints are extremely sheer too, so it works with basically every lip liner I pair it with.

Where skincare and makeup come to play, this foundation feels like a smooth gel cream that melts into the skin like butter. Available in 32 shades, you can build the coverage of this foundation up or keep it as minimal as you’d like. As for its ingredients, hydration is the name of the game with a mix of squalane and glycerin.

Lip Line is one of my favorite lip liners ever, and I own more than 50 (sorry, I’m a lip liner fiend). I love how easily the formula glides onto my lips, but the best part is how long it lasts. I don’t always want a stain, but I do often want a liner I don’t have to reapply right away. These stay on for hours without needing to pull it out of my bag and re-do, and they do so without drying out my lips.

As a lipstick lover, Ultralip remains a top-tier product. Looking in the mirror and seeing your under-eyes creased is a top-five woe of makeup users all around. Stretch Balm concealer is flexible, lightweight, and hydrating. Let’s be real: Not all cleansers easily take off all of your makeup in one go. What can we say, we’re fans of the classics! Balm Dotcom is one of the brand’s best-selling products, and for good reason. “Let the record show that Balm Dot Calm is still one of the best lip balms out there, despite having spawned hundreds of copycats since it first took over our feeds,” says commerce writer Sarah Maberry. “Old-school Glossier fans will be happy to hear they returned to the OG formula but kept the new and improved packaging. For years, I've kept a few of the birthday cake flavor on hand for an easy last-minute gift that everyone loves. I've even had friends tell me they look forward to their annual restock.”

If you wish you could bathe in Glossier You, you’ll enjoy dousing yourself in this body butter. It’s rich and decadent as it hydrates skin with shea butter and jojoba oil. I keep the chic jar on my nightstand and coat my skin with this cream before bed, and it makes my skin soft and supple (and smell amazing).

#6779. Blade Runner 2099 Ends on a Touching Note About Empathy

Blade Runner 2099 might not be getting a second season, but the show’s final episode provided a tidy ending for everyone involved. The final episode sees the show’s main characters, Cora and Olwen (played by Hunter Schafer and Michelle Yeoh, respectively) reaching the Tyrell Launch Complex on a quest to find out where Tyrell’s memory is located.

The journey isn’t without its twists and turns: One person who is the key to obtaining Tyrell’s memory winds up dead, and Olwen’s future hangs in the balance as she gets closer to the end of her lifespan. Cora’s life as a Replicant also has a few complications of its own, too.

Here’s what happened in the season finale of Blade Runner 2099.

Olwen and Cora spend a large portion of the final episode searching for Tyrell’s memory at the Tyrell Launch Complex, which belongs to replicant creator Eldon Tyrell and serves as documentation about Nexus-1 replicants Julius and Helena.

Inside the complex, Olwen and Cora split up. Olwen finds Clotilde and they talk about how Julius killed her. When Clotilde suffers a fall, Olwen doesn’t allow her to die again; in exchange for saving her, Clotilde shares where Julius is within the complex.

Meanwhile, Julius discovers Cora’s whereabouts in the complex. Shortly after, Julius and Cora fight, and he inflicts a serious stab wound on her. He also destroys Tyrell’s memory and insists that he’s the only one who can extend Olwen’s life, but Olwen finds the pair, jumps in, and kills Julius with a gunshot.

Olwen spends the majority of the series aware that she’s at the end of her lifespan. As a Replicant, she was given a fixed limit to how long she can live and has accepted her fate—but she’s offered a second chance at life by the end of the series.

After saving Clotilde, she later reveals that she saw Tyrell’s memory before he died and knows how to re-create Olwen as a Nexus-1. Clotilde re-creates Olwen in exchange for Olwen having saved Clotilde’s life. By the end of the episode, Olwen emerges from a birthing bag, and she later leaves Earth on a spaceship.

The series ends with Cora and Greta understanding each other. Cora, a human posing as a Replicant, heads back to LAPD and is given a Replicant test by Greta to confirm her identity, but this time, Cora turns the questions on Greta and asks about her life.

The pair talks about Greta’s doll, leading Cora to come to the realization that the girl is still capable of understanding what it means to love and be loved. Cora becomes emotional at the realization, leading Greta to comment that Cora has high levels of empathy. This means Cora technically fails the Replicant test, but Greta allows her to continue hiding her identity and her work as a Replicant.

#6776. Broiled Salmon Teriyaki

Sometimes all it takes to make dinner feel special is a big, bold piece of protein. Case in point: This salty-sweet salmon glazed in a glossy teriyaki-style sauce. Brushed in two rounds with the quick sauce made with nothing more than sugar, soy sauce, sesame oil, and vinegar, the salmon sizzles under the broiler, charring as it takes on a smoky flavor. This recipe calls for one large piece of salmon, but you can use smaller fillets or opt for a white fish such as cod or halibut. Just note that the cooking time will be shorter if using smaller pieces, so keep an eye on them. Add a quick garnish of sliced scallions and toasted sesame seeds, and dinner is done.

More salmon winners this way: Hot Honey-Glazed Salmon; Green Curry-Glazed Salmon; and Slow-Roasted Salmon With Harissa.

Bring ⅓ cup (packed; 67 g) dark brown sugar, ¼ cup soy sauce, 2 Tbsp. unseasoned rice vinegar, and 2 tsp. toasted sesame oil to a simmer in a small saucepan over medium-high heat; cook until reduced by half and syrupy, 5–7 minutes. Let sauce cool until thickened slightly, about 10 minutes.

Heat broiler (if broiler is in your oven, place rack in upper third). Season both sides of one 1½–2-lb. skinless or skin-on center-cut salmon fillet with kosher salt. Place, skin side down, in a skillet or baking dish. Transfer one third of sauce to a small bowl and set aside for serving. Brush about half of remaining sauce over fillet. (If the salmon has a lot of room around it in the pan, line with foil to prevent runoff sauce from burning onto pan.)

Broil salmon until sauce is just starting to burn in spots, 4–7 minutes. Brush remaining sauce over fillet and broil until deeply charred and salmon is opaque all the way through, about 5 minutes.

Remove fish from oven and spoon reserved sauce over. Top with thinly sliced scallions and/or toasted sesame seeds if desired.
